status_rationale: Restored the dropped bit-bucket no-op theorem and preserved the eight reviewed non-vacuous obligations from v4; no semantic changes, no proofs, nine total theorem obligations for theorem-strength extraction.

unit.bounded_unit: PTX ISA 9.3 bounded unit `or.b32 d, a, b;` with optional predication
unit.scope_boundary: Only .b32 with optional predication is formalized. Source1 is register-only by architecture restriction, source2 is register-or-immediate in bounded scope, destination supports register or `_`; no malformed/exception behavior is added.

compliance_notes: No proofs are included in this stage.
No vacuous functional-determinism claims; determinism is stated over relation constructors.
No circular or imported-semantics claims from unrelated units.

validation_obligations.title: Bounded instruction shape and operand ordering
validation_obligations.description: OrB32Instruction fields are (guard, d, a, b) with source1 register-only and source2 register-or-immediate, matching bounded or syntax and architecture restriction.

validation_obligations.title: 32-bit value and minimal machine state
validation_obligations.description: B32 uses a 2^32 domain and MachineState contains value predicate files with partial lookup via Option.

validation_obligations.title: No bypass constructs or axioms
validation_obligations.description: Lean declarations are executable, definitionally transparent, and contain no sorry/admit/axiom/unsafe usage.

theorem_obligations.intent: For fixed state and instruction, OrB32Step determines at most one post-state.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If OrB32Step relates s to both s1 and s2, then s1 and s2 are equal.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32_OrB32Step_deterministic (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s1 s2 : MachineState) (h1 : OrB32Step s i s1) (h2 : OrB32Step s i s2) : s1 = s2
strength_risks: Both constructors are syntactically disjoint; proof must handle constructor mismatch with inconsistent guard equations.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The relation has both constructors in well-formed non-total states, so this is a substantive uniqueness theorem for the operational relation.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Split on h1 and h2; constructor mismatch contradicts guard equalities, same constructor reduces to constructor-level equality.

theorem_obligations.intent: Executed outcomes from execOrB32 are exactly represented by executed transitions in OrB32Step.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If execOrB32 returns executed state s', then OrB32Step s i s' holds.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32_execOrB32_executed_soundness (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) : execOrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') -> OrB32Step s i s'
theorem_obligations.conclusion: execOrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') -> OrB32Step s i s'
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The executed branch is partial but real in guarded well-defined states, so this links concrete execution output to the relation constructor.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold execOrB32 and extract constructor premises on guard/source reads.

theorem_obligations.intent: Characterize notExecuted function outcomes by false predicate and unchanged post-state.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For any s, i, and post-state s', execOrB32 returns notExecuted s' exactly when predication evaluates false and s' = s.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32_execOrB32_notExecuted_iff_false_guard (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) : execOrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.notExecuted s') ↔ (evalGuard s i.guard = some false ∧ s' = s)
theorem_obligations.conclusion: execOrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.notExecuted s') ↔ (evalGuard s i.guard = some false ∧ s' = s)
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The false-guard branch is explicit in the bounded semantics and produces a concrete state-preserving outcome, so this is non-trivial.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold execOrB32; cases on evalGuard and simplify impossible branches.

theorem_obligations.intent: Every step result is represented by execOrB32 with either executed or notExecuted outcome for the same post-state.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If OrB32Step s i s' holds, then execOrB32 s i is some outcome and that outcome is either executed s' or notExecuted s'.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32_OrB32Step_implies_execOrB32_or_notExecuted (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (h : OrB32Step s i s') : ∃ out, execOrB32 s i = some out ∧ (out = ExecOutcome.executed s' ∨ out = ExecOutcome.notExecuted s')
theorem_obligations.conclusion: ∃ out, execOrB32 s i = some out ∧ (out = ExecOutcome.executed s' ∨ out = ExecOutcome.notExecuted s')
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Partial semantics may return none, executed, or notExecuted; this lemma precisely covers both realizable relation outcomes.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Split the OrB32Step constructor cases and choose out from the matching execOrB32 branch.

theorem_obligations.intent: When execOrB32 returns none, there is no valid one-step transition, and vice versa.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: execOrB32 s i = none if and only if there is no MachineState s' with OrB32Step s i s'.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32_execOrB32_none_iff_no_step (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) : execOrB32 s i = none ↔ ¬ ∃ s', OrB32Step s i s'
theorem_obligations.conclusion: execOrB32 s i = none ↔ ¬ ∃ s', OrB32Step s i s'
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: This captures malformed-state partiality exactly for missing predicate/source inputs, which exists by construction of the bounded model.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Forward/backward by unfolding execOrB32 and inverting constructor premises.

theorem_obligations.intent: False predication leaves the machine state unchanged in the relation transition.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If a one-step relation uses post-state s' and predication is false, then s' equals s.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32_OrB32Step_false_guard_no_change (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (h : OrB32Step s i s') (hfalse : evalGuard s i.guard = some false) : s' = s
hypotheses: hfalse : evalGuard s i.guard = some false
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: This is a concrete property for the no-op branch and depends on predication semantics, not a generic relation tautology.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Use h to show constructor must be notExecuted and conclude by constructor index equality.

theorem_obligations.intent: Predicates are never modified by this unit across both relation constructors.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For any OrB32Step, every predicate register maps to the same value before and after the step.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32_OrB32Step_preserves_predicates (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (h : OrB32Step s i s') : ∀ p, s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Predicate-register maps are explicit state fields in the bounded model, so this checks that the transition has no hidden predicate writes.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Split h into constructors; notExecuted is reflexive, executed reduces through updateDestination which only touches valueRegs.

theorem_obligations.intent: Only the destination register may change; any other value register preserves its mapping.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: Given OrB32Step and register r not equal to destination register (if destination is a register), valueRegs r is unchanged.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32_OrB32Step_value_reg_frame_nonDest (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (r : RegId) (h : OrB32Step s i s') (hd : i.d ≠ Destination.reg r) : s'.valueRegs r = s.valueRegs r
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The update function writes only through destination; this excludes unintended writes to unrelated value registers while permitting destination replacement.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Split h into notExecuted/executed cases and unfold updateDestination.

theorem_obligations.intent: A relation step with destination _ leaves machine state unchanged.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For any OrB32Step with i.d = Destination.bitBucket, the post-state equals pre-state.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32_OrB32Step_bitBucket_noop (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (h : OrB32Step s i s') (hd : i.d = Destination.bitBucket) : s' = s
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Bit-bucket is supported in the bounded destination syntax and mapped to an explicit no-op update design choice, so this checks that the relation respects that constructor semantics.
strength_risks: This theorem is a design/architecture property (not an NVIDIA or.b32 source fact) and should remain attributed as such.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Use h to identify constructor; apply hd to reduce to `Destination.bitBucket` branch of updateDestination in executed or reflexive notExecuted branch when applicable.
